unlisted_practices: Develop global data-sharing frameworks that maintain patient privacy.
Develop explainable AI models to improve interpretability and foster trust among clinicians and patients.
Promote collaboration among AI researchers, oncologists, and regulatory agencies so AI-derived biomarkers can be used in clinical practice with confidence.
Address class imbalance in oncological datasets to alleviate algorithmic bias.
Involve diverse datasets and expert participation during development and implementation to eliminate bias in radiology AI.

Address data accessibility and privacy through consent strategies, privacy risk assessment, cryptographic approaches for querying clinical data, and game-theoretic methods for publishing summary information.
Manage statistical uncertainty in AI cancer diagnostics through robust data collection, cross-validation, uncertainty quantification, explainable AI, and continuous learning.
Improve diversity in cancer clinical trials through culturally sensitive outreach, education, and dissemination of accessible research within local communities.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/letter outlining AI applications in biomarker discovery for cancer diagnosis and prognosis, discussing challenges and ethical issues.
